rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly scene is a divinely imposed trial, so the Prophet should not grieve over people absorbed in its pleasures; they cannot defeat God's will, and only deeds endure.
rows.anchor: فمحصل معنى الآية لا تتحرج ولا تأسف عليهم إذا عرضوا عن دعوتك بالإنذار والتبشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barren plain is a metaphor for severing human attachment to earthly possessions and adornments when their trial ends.
rows.anchor: والمراد به قطع رابطة التعلق بين الإنسان وبين أمتعة الحياة الدنيا مما على الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the image literally: the earth's adornment will become level dust, smooth and barren of growth or anything attractive.
rows.anchor: المراد به حقيقة معنى الصعيد الجرز، والمعنى أنا سنعيد ما على الأرض من زينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ما عليها replaces an expected pronoun, perhaps to stress that the adornment lies upon the earth.
rows.anchor: من قبيل وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر وكان من طبع الكلام أن يقال وإنا لجاعلوه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits through al-Barqī and Abū Baṣīr from al-Bāqir that the severe warning is ʿAlī, who fought the Prophet's enemy; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies this as application, not exegesis.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام { لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه } قال البأس الشديد علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report identifying the severe warning with ʿAlī is an application of the verse, not its interpretation; Ibn Shahrāshūb also transmits it from al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq.
rows.anchor: أقول ورواه ابن شهر آشوب عن الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام وهو من التطبيق وليس بتفسير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummī, through Abū al-Jārūd from al-Bāqir, glosses baakhiʿ nafsaka as killing oneself in grief over them and asaf as sorrow.
rows.anchor: في حديث أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { فلعلك باخع نفسك } يقول قاتل نفسك على آثارهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr reports from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet defines the best deed as greatest understanding, strongest restraint from God's prohibitions, and quickest obedience.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هذه الآية { لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Qummī's report through Abū al-Jārūd, al-Bāqir explains ṣaʿīdan juruzan as land with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { صعيدا جرزا } قال لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parables expose wealth and children as deceptive, swiftly vanishing ornaments that distract from God and leave their possessor with only a dream when destroyed; this clarifies 18:7–8.
rows.anchor: تتضمن مثلين يبينان حقيقة ما يملكه الإنسان في حياته الدنيا من الأموال والأولاد وهي زخارف الحياة وزيناتها الغارة السريعة الزوال

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators treat the two-garden story as an imagined example whose events need not have occurred.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن الذي يتضمنه المثل قصة مقدرة مفروضة فليس من الواجب أن يتحقق مضمون المثل خارجا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other commentators regard the garden story as a real event and transmit many conflicting accounts that the author says are unreliable.
rows.anchor: وذكر آخرون أنه قصة واقعة، وقد رووا في ذلك قصصا كثيرة مختلفة لا معول عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens, grapevines, surrounding palms, and crop between them support reading the story as an actual event.
rows.anchor: غير أن التدبر في سياق القصة بما فيها من كونهما جنتين اثنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are vineyards; fruit can name its tree, palms encircle both gardens, and the crop between them completes the cultivated food supply.
rows.anchor: أي من كروم فالثمرة كثيرا ما يطلق على شجرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akl means edible produce; each garden bore its grapes and dates without losing any of its productive capacity, and a river was run through both for easy irrigation.
rows.anchor: الأكل بضمتين المأكول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar most plausibly refers to the man's kinds of wealth, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ and al-Qāmūs; the author next allows the palm-fruit reading.
rows.anchor: الضمير للرجل والثمر أنواع المال كما في الصحاح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes thamar as the fruit of the palm trees.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للنخل والثمر ثمره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative says the man owned wealth apart from the gardens.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد كان للرجل ثمر ملكه من غير جنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens may have reached full ripeness, while thamar may denote fruit actually on the trees in summer; this reading avoids strain.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد من إيتاء الجنتين أكلها من غير ظلم بلوغ أشجارهما في الرشد مبلغ الإثمار وأوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāwara is reciprocal speech; nafar denotes people accompanying someone, hence its gloss as servants and children or as clan and kin.
rows.anchor: المحاورة المخاطبة والمراجعه في الكلام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some gloss nafar as servants and children.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسره بعضهم بالخدم والولد

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others gloss nafar as the man's clan and kin group.
rows.anchor: وآخرون بالرهط والعشيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants-and-children gloss fits better because the companion later contrasts his own lesser wealth and children with the boast.
rows.anchor: والأول أوفق بما سيحكيه الله تعالى من قول صاحبه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rich man's boast reveals assumed self-sufficiency: he forgets God granted and still owns his wealth, treats worldly causes as independent, and grows proud; this is latent shirk like Qārūn's claim of earning wealth by knowledge.
rows.anchor: فحسب أنه منقطع عن ربه مستقل بنفسه فيما يملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four pronouns refer to the man; garden is singular generically, perhaps because he enters each garden separately, or because the pair together is his only worldly garden.
rows.anchor: الضمائر الأربع راجعة إلى الرجل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation says the singular reflects that one cannot enter both gardens at once, but enters them successively.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن الدخول لا يتحقق في الجنتين معا في وقت واحد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the single garden means all that belongs to him: his worldly estate is his only garden, since he has no share in the promised Paradise; the author calls this a subtle reading.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت فلم أفرد الجنة بعد التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wrongs himself through arrogance toward his companion, self-admiration, latent shirk by forgetting God, and reliance on visible causes.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان ظالما لأنه تكبر على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bād and baydūda mean destruction and extinction; this refers to the garden, and the clause is separated as an answer to an implied question about what he said.
rows.anchor: البيد والبيدودة الهلاك والفناء والإشاره بهذه إلى الجنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he does not suppose the garden will perish implies permanence so secure that its destruction never enters his mind; people attach to apparent permanence and react to fortune with complacency or despair.
rows.anchor: ونفي الظن بأمر كناية عن كونه فرضا وتقديرا لا يلتفت إليه حتى يظن به ويمال إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitrah's attachment to worldly adornment is a test; once people turn from remembrance, desire and long hopes keep them fixed on present goods and visible causes against reason's warning of change and death.
rows.anchor: والسبب في ذلك كله ما أودعه الله في فطرته من التعلق بهذه الزينة الفانية فتنة وامتحانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man says he does not suppose the garden will perish rather than flatly asserting it will not, expressing the subjective presumption produced by worldly attachment; that presumption makes the Hour seem unlikely.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال فيما حكاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All human capacities and effects, from dust and semen to mature personhood, are wholly God's gift; neither people nor natural causes own these independently, so the believer rebukes the man's denial of divine lordship.
rows.anchor: فليس للإنسان أن يستقل عنه تعالى في شيء من نفسه وآثار نفسه ولا لشيء من الأسباب الكونية ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion's appeal to the man's origin in dust and semen shows that his mature humanity and powers were bestowed by God, leaving no basis for self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: يقول إنك ذاك التراب ثم المني الذي ما كان يملك من الإنسانية والرجولية وآثار ذلك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading لكنّا has a doubled open nūn in liaison and alif at pause, from لكن أنا after hamza deletion and vowel transfer; the repeated my Lord replaces an expected pronoun to explain why association is forbidden.
rows.anchor: حذفت الهمزة بعد نقل فتحتها إلى النون وأدغمت النون في النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second explicit my Lord, where the syntax could have said with Him, stresses the reason: no partner is associated with Him because He is Lord.
rows.anchor: وقد كرر في الآية لفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses continue the contrast with worldly adornment: causes and ornaments vanish, leaving each person with deeds; the gathering, Iblīs episode, failed partners, and promises form one connected sequence.
rows.anchor: الأسباب الظاهرية وزخارف الدنيا الغارة زينة الحياة سيسرع إليها الزوال ويتبين للإنسان أنها لا تملك له نفعا ولا ضرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time expression has an implicit remember; moving the mountains means removing them from their places, as other verses describe them as shifting, wool-like, scattered dust, or mirage.
rows.anchor: وتسيير الجبال بزوالها عن مستقرها وقد عبر سبحانه عنه بتعبيرات مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's becoming exposed follows the mountains' removal: no region is hidden from another, and the wording may also evoke the earth lit by its Lord's light.
rows.anchor: والمستفاد من السياق أن بروز الأرض مترتب على تسيير الجبال فإذا زالت الجبال والتلال ترى الأرض بارزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering is universal: no one is left behind.
rows.anchor: أي لم نترك منهم أحدا فالحشر عام للجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those presented are the polytheists who trusted themselves and visible causes, ignored whether their deeds pleased God, and imagined worldly ornaments would last; after the appointed term only God, themselves, and their records remain.
rows.anchor: السياق يشهد على أن ضمير الجمع في قوله { عرضوا } وكذا ضميرا الجمع في الآية السابقة للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stand in one row without distinctions of wealth, lineage, or status, seeing that worldly ornaments and their supposed independence were illusions and that they erred by imagining no reckoning awaited them.
rows.anchor: صفا واحدا لا تفاضل بينهم بنسب أو مال أو جاه دنيوي لفصل القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four selected clauses summarize judgment: presentation, return as at first creation, their denial of an appointment, and placement of the record.
rows.anchor: وبهذا البيان يظهر أن هذه الجمل الأربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presentation means a compelled meeting without honor; saying your Lord rather than their Lord signals estrangement, unlike honored believers in 98:8 and 11:79.
rows.anchor: إشارة أولا إلى أنهم ملجؤون إلى الرجوع إلى ربهم ولقائه فيعرضون عليه عرضا من غير أن يختاروه لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address that they came as first created is understood as God telling them they were mistaken to cling to worldly finery instead of following His way.
rows.anchor: وقوله { لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة } مقول القول والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast introduced by rather signals that neglect of God and sin had a deeper cause: they thought no meeting for judgment would be set, like the charge in 23:115.
rows.anchor: إن اشتغالكم بالدنيا وتعلقكم بزينتها وإن كان سببا في الاعراض عن ذكرنا واقتراف الخطيئات لكن كان هناك سبب هو أقدم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting the Day of Reckoning underlies abandoning the right path and corrupt deeds.
rows.anchor: فنسيان المعاد هو الأصل في ترك الطريق وفساد العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of an appointed return can be a practical presumption shown by treating worldly life and its ornaments as permanent, or a figure for disregard and contempt of God's commands, as in 41:22.
rows.anchor: والوجه في نسبة الظن بنفي المعاد إليهم أن انقطاعهم إلى الدنيا وتعلقهم بزينتها ومن يدعونه من دون الله فعل من ظن أنها دائمة باقية لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead reject an imagined excuse of ignorance; the author leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: ومن الجائز أن يكون قوله { بل زعمتم أن لن نجعل لكم موعدا } إضرابا عن اعتذار لهم مقدر بالجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ al-kitāb means setting the record up for judgment; ishfāq combines care with fear, with fear emphasized after min and care after fī.
rows.anchor: وضع الكتاب نصبه ليحكم عليه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains ishfāq as care mixed with fear, noting that its sense shifts toward fear with min and care with fī.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الإشفاق عناية مختلطة بخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on woe at disaster figures a calamity worse than destruction, as if ruin might rescue one from it; people may similarly wish for death, as in 19:23.
rows.anchor: والويل الهلاك، ونداؤه عند المصيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular collective record does not exclude individual, communal, and universal records; the author cites 17:13 and 45:28–29, but rejects the alternative that the definite book simply means all books because context resists it.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه كتاب واحد يوضع لحساب أعمال الجميع ولا ينافي ذلك وضع كتاب خاص بكل إنسان والآيات القرآنية دالة على أن لكل إنسان كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals' fear of the record shows it contains their deeds and extends the ruling to every wrongdoer, including those who are not polytheists.
rows.anchor: وذكرهم بوصف الإجرام للإشارة إلى علة الحكم وأن إشفاقهم مما فيه لكونهم مجرمين فالحكم يعم كل مجرم وإن لم يكن مشركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Small and great stand for sins or misdeeds; their exclamation expresses astonishment at the record's exhaustive accounting, with small named first because even minute sins being counted is startling.
rows.anchor: الصغيرة والكبيرة وصفان قامتا مقام موصوفهما وهو الخطيئة أو المعصية أو الهنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order from small to great means neither tiny and subtle nor large and obvious is omitted; that order suits their astonishment better than a climax from great to small.
rows.anchor: لا يغادر صغيرة لصغرها ودقتها ولا كبيرة لكبرها ووضوحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding their deeds present is an independent assertion, not a restatement of the book's complete tally; the deeds themselves appear in fitting forms, not merely their written notation.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق كون الجملة تأسيسا لا عطف تفسير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take the book as books of deeds, with the definite article expressing generic comprehensiveness; the author says the context does not support this.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالكتاب كتب الأعمال واللام للاستغراق، والسياق لا يساعد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding denial of injustice fits the embodiment of deeds, since people receive what they themselves did rather than something inflicted by another.
rows.anchor: فإن انتفاء الظلم بناء على تجسم الأعمال أوضح لأن ما يجزون به إنما هو عملهم يرد إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam episode reminds people that Iblīs, from the jinn, rebelled after the command to bow; he and his offspring are enemies who entice humanity toward worldly lusts and away from God.
rows.anchor: تذكير ثان لهم بما جرى بينه تعالى وبين إبليس حين أمر الملائكة بالسجود لأبيهم آدم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators explain taking Iblīs and his offspring as allies as obeying them in what they invite people to do.
rows.anchor: وهكذا فسرها المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also allows alliance to mean accepting their lordship and governance: idolaters worship angels for benefit and jinn to avert harm; the next verse supports this reading by denying their role in creation.
rows.anchor: وليس من البعيد أن يكون المراد بالولاية ولاية الملك والتدبير وهو الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them a bad substitute condemns replacing God with Iblīs; shifts from our order to his Lord and from us to Me intensify the rebuke.
rows.anchor: وهو السر في الالتفات الذي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer to Iblīs and his offspring; witness means actual presence and direct disclosure, while ʿaḍud is literally an arm and figuratively a helper.
rows.anchor: والعضد ما بين المرفق والكتف من الإنسان ويستعار للمعين كاليد وهو المراد ها هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First proof against their cosmic governance: rule requires complete knowledge of affairs and their relations, but Iblīs and his offspring never witnessed creation and are ignorant of its realities; bounded beings cannot know what lies beyond themselves.
rows.anchor: ولاية تدبير أمور شيء من الأشياء تتوقف على الإحاطة العلمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a demonstrative proof distinguishing true cosmic governance and direct knowledge of the unseen from human management, conjectures, and inference from likely signs.
rows.anchor: وهذه حجه برهانية غير جدلية عند من أجاد النظر وأمعن في التدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second proof: creatures are innately guided toward their kind's perfection, as 20:50 states; because devils mislead, using them as helpers in governance would contradict God's universal guidance.
rows.anchor: كل نوع من أنواع المخلوقات متوجه بفطرته نحو كماله المختص بنوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's first-person wording, I did not show them and I did not take them as helpers, stresses His mastery over them; idolaters claim delegated divine authority for partners rather than independence.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنه سبحانه هو القاهر المهيمن عليهم على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred interpretation reads witnessing literally and refers both pronouns to Iblīs and his offspring.
rows.anchor: مبني على حمل الإشهاد على معناه الحقيقي وإرجاع الضميرين في { ما أشهدتهم } و { أنفسهم } إلى إبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take witnessing as metaphorical consultation in creation, with denial of help then excluding their authority; the author rejects this for lack of a contextual cue or a real link between consultation and governance.
rows.anchor: إن المراد من الإشهاد في خلقها المشاورة مجازا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view treats consultation as a figure whose implication is that God created them as they wished, hence perfectly, and so potentially able to govern; the author rejects its chain of several strained implications.
rows.anchor: بأن المراد بالإشهاد المشاورة كنايه ولازم المشاورة أن يخلق كما شاؤا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That figurative reading also splits the two witnessing clauses, would grant possible authority to perfectly created angels, and conflicts with the Qur'an's denial that dependent beings govern themselves or others.
rows.anchor: وثالثا أن لازمه صحة ولاية من كان كاملا في خلقه كالملائكة المقربين ففيه اعتراف بإمكان ولايتهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some retain literal witnessing and say devils witnessed one another's creation; the author rejects this because the point is to deny governance, and no polytheists claim devils govern each other.
rows.anchor: لكن المراد من إشهادهم خلق أنفسهم إشهاد بعضهم خلق بعض لا إشهاد كل خلق نفسه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view assigns the first pronoun to devils and the second to unbelievers or people, meaning the devils did not witness their creation; the author rejects the pronoun split.
rows.anchor: إن أول الضميرين للشياطين والثاني للكفار أو لهم ولغيرهم من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase al-mudabbirāt amran at 79:5 will be explained later in the commentary.
rows.anchor: فالمدبرات أمرا النازعات 5 فسيجيء توضيح معناه إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers both pronouns to refer to unbelievers who demanded the Prophet dismiss poor followers, arguing they had no role in cosmic governance and so could not make such demands.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الرازي في تفسيره والأقرب عندي عودهما يعني الضميرين على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls al-Rāzī's interpretation very remote: it breaks the passage's flow, and the unbelievers' condition that poor people be expelled is not a claim to participate in managing the world.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن فيه خرق السياق بتعليق مضمون الآية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other attempts say the unbelievers lacked knowledge of predestination or were not specially informed about creation and thus could not be exemplary; the author says both are even further from the text.
rows.anchor: وكأن التنبه لهذه النكتة دعا بعضهم إلى توجيه معنى الآية على تقدير رجوع الضميرين إلى الكفار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some refer both pronouns to angels, so the verse denies their authority while its final clause denies that of devils; the author rejects this as disrupting the prior focus on Iblīs and his offspring.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن الضميرين للملائكة والمعنى ما أشهدت الملائكة خلق العالم ولا خلق أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a third reminder: on Judgment Day God exposes the broken bond between idolaters and alleged partners by telling them to summon them; their failure to answer proves they are no partners.
rows.anchor: هذا تذكير ثالث يذكر فيه ظهور بطلان الرابطة بين المشركين وبين شركائهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūbiq is a place of destruction; although commentators take it as Hell or a region of it, the author rejects that because partners include angels, prophets, and saints, not only rebellious jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر القوم هذا الموبق والمهلك بالنار أو بمحل من النار يهلك فيه الفريقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gap is the annihilation of the supposed relationship, not of either party; the call across distance hints at their separation, as in 6:94 and 10:28.
rows.anchor: فلعل المراد من جعل موبق بينهم إبطال الرابطة ورفعها من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them criminals rather than polytheists makes the judgment apply to all wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: في أخذ المجرمين مكان المشركين دلالة على أن الحكم عام لجميع أهل الإجرام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read their supposition as certain knowledge, which is supported by their finding no place to escape.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالظن هو العلم - على ما قيل - ويشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūqiʿūhā means falling into Hell; it may also imply mutual involvement, as they enter the fire and it burns within them.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون المراد حصول الوقوع من الجانبين فهم واقعون في النار بدخولهم فيها والنار واقعة فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣrif, with kasra on the rāʾ, is a place of turning aside: they find no destination or escape from the fire.
rows.anchor: المصرف بكسر الراء اسم مكان من الصرف أي لم يجدوا محلا ينصرفون إليه ويعدلون عن النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening resembles 17:89; the following six verses threaten punishment after the preceding reminders, and jadal means contentious disputation.
rows.anchor: قد مر الكلام في نظير صدر الآية في سورة الإسراء آيه 89 والجدل الكلام على سبيل المنازعة والمشاجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ask forgiveness coordinates with believe: guidance arrived, yet people were prevented from both belief and seeking forgiveness; what they effectively want is extermination like earlier peoples or visible punishment that forces useless late faith, as in 40:85.
rows.anchor: أي وما منعهم من الإيمان والاستغفار حين مجيء الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's stated obstacle is rhetorical: their corrupt inward state makes them turn from truth, so there is no need to belabor objections about the grammatical ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وهذا المنع والاقتضاء في الآية أمر ادعائي يراد به أنهم معرضون عن الحق لسوء سريرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The message consoles the Prophet: messengers only bring good news and warning, so he should not be distressed by rejection; it also warns mockers. Daḥḍ means destruction or invalidation, and huzūʾ is ridicule.
rows.anchor: تعزية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن لا يضيق صدره من إنكار المنكرين وإعراضهم عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their injustice is supreme because it is directed against God through His signs; forgetting their deeds means disregarding their known rejection and mockery.
rows.anchor: والظلم يعظم ويكبر بحسب متعلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering on hearts and heaviness in ears explains their turning away and forgetting; they cannot recognize truth by reflection or follow another's guidance, and if called they will never be guided.
rows.anchor: كأنه تعليل لإعراضهم عن آيات الله أوله ولنسيانهم ما قدمت أيديهم

rows.speaker: الجبريّة والقدريّة
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says determinists and proponents of human agency each cite one of the adjacent verses, calling this a divine test distinguishing learned scholars from imitators.
rows.anchor: قال في روح المعاني واستدلت الجبرية بهذه الآية على مذهبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both verses are true: humans choose their acts while God's sovereignty extends throughout His dominion, including those acts, the position of the Imams of the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: أقول وكلتا الآيتين حق ولازم ذلك ثبوت الاختيار للعباد في أعمالهم وانبساط سلطنته تعالى في ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though their corrupt deeds warrant immediate punishment, God delays the certain punishment to a term fixed by His knowledge because He is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: لكن الله سبحانه لم يعجل لهم العذاب وإن قضى به قضاء حتم بل أخره إلى أجل مسمى عينه بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's forgiveness and mercy defer punishment while the appointed term makes it binding and inescapable; the wording is a judicial decree, not mere narration.
rows.anchor: كلمة قضاء وليس بحكاية محضة وإلا قيل بل جعل لهم موعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafūr intensifies frequent forgiveness, while dhu al-raḥma uses the genus of mercy and is broader than al-Raḥmān or al-Raḥīm; forgiveness clears impediments so comprehensive mercy can reach its recipients.
rows.anchor: والغفور صيغة مبالغة تدل على كثرة المغفرة، وذو الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns means their inhabitants by metonymy, as shown by the pronouns, and mahlak with kasra on the lām denotes a time.
rows.anchor: المراد بالقرى أهلها مجازا بدليل الضمائر الراجعة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that delayed destruction is God's established way with earlier unjust peoples: He gives their destruction an appointed time.
rows.anchor: السنة الإلهية في الأمم الماضين الذين أهلكهم الله لما ظلموا كانت جارية على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment here is worldly: the Battle of Badr if Quraysh's leaders are meant, or an end-times punishment if the broader community is meant.
rows.anchor: عذاب دنيوي وهو عذاب يوم بدر إن كان المراد تهديد صناديد قريش أو عذاب آخر الزمان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Khālid ibn Najīḥ, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, that the person recalls every moment, word, step, and deed in the record as if done that hour; the author says such recollection makes the proof undeniable.
rows.anchor: عن خالد بن نجيح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا كان يوم القيامة دفع للإنسان كتابه ثم قيل له اقرأ

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummī explains that the denial of injustice means people will find everything they did written down.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا يظلم ربك أحدا } قال يجدون كل ما عملوا مكتوبا

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Burhān transmits through Ibn Bābawayh and Abū Maʿmar al-Saʿdān from ʿAlī that ẓannū means they were certain they would enter Hell.
rows.anchor: عن ابن بابويه بإسناده عن أبي معمر السعدان عن علي عليه السلام قال قوله { ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها } أي أيقنوا أنهم داخلوها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr reports from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that the unbeliever stands for fifty thousand years as if never alive, and sees Hell from forty years away believing he will enter; al-Ḥākim graded the report sound.
rows.anchor:
عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال
" ينصب الكافر يوم القيامة مقدار خمسين ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report supports the reading that mūqiʿa describes mutual involvement between people and the fire.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو يؤيد ما تقدم أن المواقعة في الآية مأخوذة بين الأثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses and learned-servant story is a fourth reminder: outward worldly success has a hidden interpretation under divine authority, revealed when the present trial ends and people awaken to another life.
rows.anchor: فالتذكير بقصة موسى والعالم كأنه للإشارة إلى أن لهذه الوقائع والحوادث التي تجري على مشتهى أهل الدنيا تأويلا سيظهر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is Ibn ʿImrān, the messenger and one of the resolute prophets, as Shīʿī and Sunnī reports say; the alternative Moses son of Mīshā, a descendant of Joseph, is unlikely because the Qur'an uses Moses for Ibn ʿImrān over 130 times without a clarifying cue.
rows.anchor: وموسى الذي ذكر في القصة هو ابن عمران الرسول النبي أحد أولي العزم عليه السلام على ما وردت به الرواية من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some treat the story as a fictional allegory in which perfect knowledge leads to a fountain of life and eternal happiness; the author rejects this as unsupported and absent from the Qur'anic account.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن القصة أسطورة تخييلية صورت لغاية أن كمال المعرفة يورد الإنسان مشرعة عين الحياة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The companion called Moses' youth is said to be Joshua son of Nun, his legatee, called youth either because he accompanied Moses or served him.
rows.anchor: والفتى الذي ذكره الله وأضافه إلى موسى قيل هو يوشع بن نون وصيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports name the learned servant al-Khiḍr and call him a prophet contemporary with Moses; claims that he remains alive are acceptable absent decisive contrary evidence, though many later stories are fabricated or contaminated.
rows.anchor: ورد في الروايات أن اسمه الخضر وكان نبيا من الأنبياء معاصر لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause has an implicit remember and coordinates with earlier reminders. Lā abraḥ means continue, with an omitted predicate supplied as travel; the meeting of the seas is identified by some as the eastern Mediterranean and western Persian Sea, and ḥuquban means a long time.
rows.anchor: بمعنى لا أزال وهو من الأفعال الناقصة حذف خبره إيجازا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some locate the meeting of the seas where the Mediterranean ends to the east and the Persian Sea to the west.
rows.anchor: ومجمع البحرين قيل { هو الذي ينتهي إليه بحر الروم من الجانب الشرقي وبحر الفرس من الجانب الغربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ḥuqban implies an omitted adjective, meaning a long time; Moses vows to travel until he reaches the meeting point or spends a long while.
rows.anchor: والحقب الدهر والزمان وتنكيره يدل على وصف محذوف والتقدير حقبا طويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majmaʿ baynahumā is a construct where a descriptive phrase stands for the described noun: the meeting point of the two seas.
rows.anchor: من إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف وأصله بين البحرين الموصوف بأنه مجمعهما

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A common account says they carried a salted or roasted dead fish as provisions; it revived at the meeting point, entered the sea, and the youth saw it but forgot to tell Moses, while Moses forgot to ask.
rows.anchor: فموسى نسي كونه في المكتل فلم يتفقده والفتى نسيه إذ لم يخبر موسى بعجيب ما رأى من أمره. هذا ما ذكروه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses do not explicitly say the fish revived; the wording permits that it fell or was carried from the rock into the sea and vanished into its depths like a tunnel, and some reports make its absence—not its life—the sign.
rows.anchor: أن الآيات غير صريحه في حياه الحوت بعد ما كان ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forgot the fish in different senses: Moses forgot it was in the basket, while the youth forgot to report what he had seen.
rows.anchor: فموسى نسي كونه في المكتل فلم يتفقده والفتى نسيه إذ لم يخبر موسى بعجيب ما رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saraban means a path or passage, especially a tunnel dug into earth; the fish's underwater route is likened to a tunnel where a traveler disappears.
rows.anchor: السرب المسلك والمذهب والسرب والنفق الطريق المحفور في الأرض لا نفاذ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab, waṣab, and fatigue are synonyms for weakness from exertion; ghidāʾ means the meal eaten at midday, showing the travel occurred during the day.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع النصب والوصب والتعب نظائر، وهو الوهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After passing the meeting point, Moses asks for their fish meal because the journey has tired them; the youth explains that the fish entered the sea when they reached the rock, and that he forgot to tell Moses.
rows.anchor: يقول لموسى لا غداء عندنا نتغدى به فإن غداءنا وهو الحوت حي ودخل البحر وذهب حينما بلغنا مجمع البحرين
